meta.subtitle: Grid-led growth and the Comtrafo deal, with the shares in the lower part of their 52-week range

analystSentiment.commentary:
At $30.01 the shares trade much nearer the 52-week low of $24.87 than the high of $70.49.

The operating record does not read like a broken story. Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 rose {+ +30.0% +} year over year to $94.1M, at an operating margin of 10.5%.

The case rests on the operating line, not on reported net income, for the reasons set out in Financials. Valuation sets out the three scenarios, their anchors and the weighting behind the call.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
American Superconductor Corporation, incorporated in 1987 and headquartered in Ayer, Massachusetts, sells megawatt-scale power resiliency products through two segments the 10-Q names Grid and Wind. Grid serves utilities, industrial facilities, renewable developers and U.S. and allied Navies with products such as D-VAR systems, transformers and ship protection systems. Wind licenses turbine designs under the Windtec Solutions brand and supplies electrical control systems and support services to turbine manufacturers.

Fiscal labels need care. The company's fiscal year ends March 31 and is named for the calendar year in which it begins, so the year ended March 31, 2026 is fiscal 2025 in the proxy statement but FY26 in the vendor tables. This report uses the vendor labels for table figures and period end dates elsewhere. The quarter ended June 30, 2026 opens the company's fiscal 2026, which is the vendor's FY27E.

Grid dominates the business: the June 18, 2026 proxy statement puts Grid at 84% of fiscal 2025 revenue. The vendor tables carry the company as a single consolidated segment, so no Wind figure is quotable here. In December 2025 the company added Comtrafo, a Brazil-based maker of power and distribution transformers, to Grid.

The evidence base is narrow: an excerpt of the 10-Q MD&A, the 10-K risk factors and the proxy statement's compensation discussion. No earnings release, call transcript or news headlines were captured, so several questions in this report stay open.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body:
The operating business is scaling: gross margin widened in each year from FY23 to FY26, operating margin turned positive in FY26, and the June 2026 quarter ran at a higher operating margin than the full year. Free cash flow has been positive in each of the last three fiscal years. The price sits below the probability-weighted value, but that upside is too thin against the Bear downside for a BUY (see Valuation).

The balance sheet is a supporting point rather than a pillar: liquidity covers current liabilities, but debt data for FY26 is missing and the Comtrafo cash outlay is not visible in the rounded tables (see Financials). The counter-case is real: reported FY26 earnings are not a run-rate, consensus EPS falls sharply into FY27E, and the Comtrafo deal adds emerging-market and integration risk.

catalysts: Next 10-Q: a September 2026 quarter that holds revenue growth and operating margin near the June-quarter levels would support the Base case (see Financials).
Backlog update: the next disclosed backlog shows whether the order growth reported for the year ended March 31, 2026 is still converting (see Growth).
Comtrafo contribution: a full year of the Brazilian transformer business inside Grid will show whether the acquisition earns its price (see Risks).
Estimate path: consensus calls for EPS to rise from FY27E to FY28E, and holding that path is what the Base case prices.
risks: Earnings quality: FY26 net income ran far above operating income, so trailing earnings overstate earnings power (see Financials).
Share-price weakness: the fall from the 52-week high is unexplained and is a driver of the Bear weight (see Valuation).
Concentration: Wind leans on a single customer and government contracts depend on appropriations (see Risks).
Emerging markets: Comtrafo deepens exposure to Brazil (see Risks).

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended March 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Revenue growth has been strong but is slowing. Vendor YoY growth ran {+ +37.4% +} in FY24, {+ +53.0% +} in FY25 and {+ +34.3% +} in FY26, reaching $299.2M, after a {- -2.3% -} dip in FY23. Consensus looks for $367.8M in FY27E, a {+ +23% +} step that would extend the deceleration.

Margins have improved each year since FY23. Gross margin rose from 8.0% in FY23 to 30.5% in FY26, and operating margin climbed from -31.1% to 3.8% over the same span. The trailing-twelve-month operating margin of 4.9% sits above the FY26 level, so the latest quarter extended the trend at the operating line. The trailing gross margin of 28.6% sits below FY26, however, and is the line to monitor in the next quarter.

Reported earnings overstate the run-rate. FY26 net income was $133.8M, and the trailing net margin of 42.6% compares with the trailing operating margin cited above, so a large item sits below the operating line that the captured text does not itemize. A 10-Q risk factor warns that "changes in valuation allowance of deferred tax assets may affect our future operating results," but it does not tie that item to FY26. The vendor shows FY26 diluted EPS of $3.05, while the June 18, 2026 proxy statement reports $3.12 per share without stating its basis; this report uses the vendor figure. Consensus EPS of $0.88 for FY27E is the better guide to earnings power, and its GAAP or non-GAAP basis is not stated.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended March 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
Liquidity is adequate rather than abundant. The FY26 current ratio was 2.39 and the trailing ratio 2.43, up from 1.26 in FY23, so current assets cover current liabilities more than twice.

The tables are too coarse to show how the Comtrafo payments changed the cash position. Cash and short-term investments round to $0.1B in each of FY24, FY25 and FY26, and the FY26 total debt and net debt cells are blank in the vendor data, which this report treats as missing rather than zero.

Total equity stepped up to $0.6B in FY26 from $0.2B in FY25. The two visible contributors are the year's net income, discussed above, and the shares issued for Comtrafo. For holders, that means equity growth came largely from a non-run-rate earnings line and from issuing stock, not from retained operating profit.

Two 10-Q risk factors bear on the balance sheet. Performance bonds can tie up cash used as collateral, and the company says "we may require additional financing in the future, which may not be available to us." The next 10-K's debt and cash disclosures are the check on whether the acquisition left the balance sheet thinner than the rounded tables suggest.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended March 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow is positive but its margin slipped in FY26. FCF was $18.3M in FY26, a 6.1% FCF margin, down from 11.6% in FY25, with no explanation in the excerpts. Both years compare with deeply negative margins of -18.4% in FY22 and -22.4% in FY23, the history behind the 10-Q's own warning that "we have a history of negative operating cash flows."

At today's price the trailing FCF yield is 1.4%, which offers little valuation support on its own. The case depends on cash generation growing with earnings; how the retained cash is deployed is covered under Management.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
The headline multiples point in opposite directions, and the trailing ones mislead. The P/E (TTM) of 9.7x rests on trailing earnings, whose net margin carries the below-the-line item discussed in Financials, so it says little about earnings power.

Forward multiples are the relevant ones. The vendor's Fwd P/E (NTM) of 34.0x lines up with the FY27E consensus EPS at today's price, so it reads as a multiple on the fiscal year now in progress rather than a strict next-twelve-months figure. On FY28E consensus EPS the stock trades at ~22.1x. Both multiples use the same consensus estimates, so the gap between them reflects the expected rise in EPS from FY27E to FY28E.

EV/EBITDA (TTM) of 56.5x and P/S of 4.5x show how thin operating earnings still are relative to sales. Those levels leave the stock exposed if margins stall. No peer multiples are available, so this report makes no relative-value claim.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: 12-month horizon. Estimates rise above consensus as margins keep widening, and the shares re-rate to the Street median target of $61.00. Requires upward revisions, not just delivery of the current consensus path.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: 12-month horizon. Revenue tracks FY27E consensus of $367.8M and FY28E consensus EPS of $1.36 is delivered. Two readings are equally likely: the stock keeps its 34.0x year-in-progress multiple on that EPS, or it keeps only the ~22.1x it carries on FY28E today, which is today's price. Base is the midpoint, about $38.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: 12-month horizon. Earnings stall at FY27E consensus EPS of $0.88 and the multiple compresses to the FY28E multiple named in Base, giving about $19.50. Consistent with backlog slippage, a loss at the main Wind customer or Comtrafo integration problems.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base is a one-year roll, not two. A year from now FY28E is the fiscal year in progress, so carrying the year-in-progress multiple discussed above onto FY28E EPS needs no expansion. That multiple, however, rests on the visible EPS step from FY27E to FY28E; a year on, consensus shows only slower revenue growth into FY28E and no FY29E estimate. The market could just as easily pay only the lower multiple it already pays on FY28E, which leaves the shares at today's level even with FY28E EPS delivered. We treat the two readings as equally likely and price Base at their midpoint; the target range runs from the flat reading at its low end to the full roll at its high end.

Bear is a different case: earnings stall at the FY27E level and the multiple compresses as well. It gets 40%, a heavy weight, for two reasons. The shares trade far below their 52-week high and no captured source explains the fall, so the market may know something the filings here do not show. FY27E consensus EPS is also a sharp step down from reported FY26 earnings. Base gets 45%. Bull gets 15% because it needs estimates to rise, not just hold.

The Street sits well above this report. All four covering analysts rate the stock Buy, with targets from $54.00 to $71.00 and a consensus of $61.75. The dates of those targets are not visible, so this report does not adopt them; the Street median anchors only the Bull case.

The weighted fair value of $34.05 gives expected upside of {+ +13.5% +} against bear-case downside of {- -35.0% -}, a reward/risk of 0.38×. On the page's own rule that derives HOLD: the upside is positive but does not cover the Bear downside by enough for a BUY.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The vendor data treats the company as one consolidated segment, while the 10-Q describes two: Grid and Wind. With Grid at the share of revenue noted in the overview, the moat question is decided in Grid: its mix of planning services, power quality systems, transformers and naval products is where pricing and margin gains must show. Wind is the smaller piece, but it depends on the manufacturers that license its designs and on the customer concentration set out in Risks, so it adds risk out of proportion to its size. No segment margin data is available, so this report draws no conclusion on which segment drives the margin gains.

moatFactors.name: Naval and government programs
moatFactors.body: Sales of ship protection and power products to U.S. and allied Navies give the company program-level relationships with government customers. The contract terms set out in Risks, including audit, termination and appropriation exposure, mean these relationships are real but not contractually durable.

moatFactors.name: Planning services pull-through
moatFactors.body: The 10-Q says the company's transmission planning services "often lead to sales of our grid interconnection solutions," which gives it an early seat in utility projects. That is the company's own description, offered without a conversion figure, so it supports the factor only modestly.

moatFactors.name: Superconductor technology
moatFactors.body: The company states it has had "limited success marketing and selling our superconductor products and system-level solutions," and warns its patents "may not provide meaningful or long-term protection." The namesake technology is not, on this evidence, a source of advantage today.

businessMoat.durability: We assign no moat. FY26 gross margin of 30.5% is far better than earlier years but is not the level of a business with pricing power, and the 10-Q lists industry consolidation that "could result in more powerful competitors and fewer customers" among its risks. Returns depend on execution, mix and acquisitions rather than a structural advantage. The test of durability is whether gross margin holds its recent gains as competition responds.

points: Grid is the engine. The proxy statement reports fiscal 2025 Grid revenue up {+ 34% +} to $251.3 million from $187.2 million and attributes the increase to "organic growth and the contribution from our acquisition" of Comtrafo. It does not split the two, so the organic growth rate cannot be read off.

Backlog is dated evidence. The June 18, 2026 proxy statement says the twelve-month backlog grew by over 40% to $282.4 million at March 31, 2026, from $200.9 million a year earlier. Any backlog figure in the August 2026 10-Q was not captured, and by October 2026 about half of that delivery window has passed, so it supports the current year only in part. The 10-K also cautions that customers can "terminate, reduce or defer firm orders."

Consensus expects deceleration, not a stall: FY28E revenue of $423.6M implies continued but slower expansion after FY27E. The consensus path the Base case needs is set out in its scenario driver in Valuation.

Acquisitions are part of the plan. The 10-K names "identifying and completing opportunistic acquisitions" as a strategic initiative, and Comtrafo extends Grid into Brazilian utility transformers. Future growth may therefore come partly from deals, whose risks are set out in Risks.

management.leadership: The June 18, 2026 proxy statement lists two named executive officers for fiscal 2025: Daniel P. McGahn, Chairman of the Board, President and Chief Executive Officer, and John W. Kosiba, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. The proxy reports that in fiscal 2025 the company achieved its seventh consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability and its eleventh consecutive quarter of generating operating cash flow. That record supports confidence in operational delivery, but it is the company's own account in a compensation document, and the excerpt carries no tenure or succession information.
management.capitalAllocation:
Capital goes to acquisitions rather than shareholder returns. For Comtrafo, the company paid 300 million Brazilian Real in cash and issued shares at closing on December 5, 2025, plus 155.6 million and 13.4 million Brazilian Real for real estate and transportation assets. It also acquired Megatran Industries in August 2024. Paying partly in stock conserves cash but dilutes existing holders; the test of whether Comtrafo earns its price is set out in Risks.

Nothing is returned to shareholders. The company pays no dividend and recorded share repurchases of $0.00 in FY26. A 10-Q risk factor adds that performance on U.S. Department of Defense contracts "may result in restrictions to our ability to repurchase our common stock," so buybacks are not a lever investors should count on.
management.governance: The proxy excerpt is limited to the Compensation Discussion and Analysis, so board composition, independence and pay levels cannot be assessed. One structural point is visible: the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer roles are combined in one person, which concentrates oversight. The 10-Q also flags that failure to maintain effective internal control over financial reporting on business acquisitions could impair timely reporting, a live consideration while Comtrafo is integrated.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy excerpt (June 18, 2026) contains no beneficial-ownership table, so insider stakes and alignment cannot be judged from ownership. The one visible new holder group is Comtrafo's sellers, who received 2,417,142 shares against ~48.44M shares outstanding (a count derived from market capitalization). That block is a small fraction of the share count, far too small to give the sellers control, so outside holders' exposure is to dilution rather than to a new controlling party.

idiosyncratic: Earnings normalization. The gap between reported net income and operating income described in Financials means trailing EPS is not a guide to FY27E. If investors anchor on trailing earnings, the step-down can disappoint. Monitor the tax line in each 10-Q and whether reported EPS tracks the consensus path.

Wind customer concentration. The 10-Q states that "a significant portion of our Wind segment revenues are derived from a single customer." A slowdown at that customer would hit Wind revenue directly. The signal is any change in Wind order flow or licensee commentary in the next filings.

Government contract terms. The 10-Q says U.S. and Canadian government contracts "are subject to audit, modification or termination" and that funding "may remain subject to annual legislative appropriation," and separately that changes in U.S. defense spending could hurt results. The proxy lists military among the markets behind fiscal 2025 orders, so a funding gap would reach backlog as well as revenue. Track Navy-related orders and appropriations timing.

Comtrafo and Brazil. The 10-Q warns that changes in Brazil's political, social, regulatory and economic environment, and in exchange rates, may affect results, and the 10-K lists "mistaken assumptions about volumes, revenues and costs" among acquisition risks. Integration missteps or a weaker Brazilian Real would weigh on Grid. The test of whether the deal earns its price is Grid margin and any foreign-currency impact disclosed over the next several quarters.
risks.systemic: Macroeconomic and trade pressure is the main external risk. The 10-Q cites the wars between Russia and Ukraine and in the Middle East, tariffs, trade restrictions and supply chain disruption as conditions that could have a material adverse effect, and separately says the conflicts between the United States, Israel, and Iran have "disrupted global energy markets and supply chains." The company relies on a limited number of qualified suppliers for components, so input-cost spikes or shortages flow quickly into margins. Wind demand also depends on "the availability and size of government subsidies" and on prices of other energy sources. The indicators to follow are supplier-cost commentary in the 10-Q and any change in U.S. trade policy affecting imported components.

body: HOLD, target range $30–$46, resting on the Base case and weighting set out in Valuation.

We would move to BUY if two further quarters show operating margin above the June-quarter level together with an upward revision to FY28E consensus EPS. We would move to SELL on a year-over-year decline in quarterly revenue, a cut to FY28E consensus EPS, or a twelve-month backlog in the next 10-K below the March 31, 2026 level.
